videos.title: Trevor Noah: What I Was Hiding Behind Every Joke
videos.description:
Who are you without the pain? Trevor Noah on why we hold on to the old version of ourselves, even when it hurts.

In this episode, Trevor Noah and Jay Shetty talk about what it means to feel lost, and how you find your way back. Trevor grew up with poverty and domestic abuse in South Africa, and for years he told himself it was not bad because it happened to everyone.

He explains why he is never grateful for suffering, why "I don't want to lose me" keeps so many of us stuck, and why a 15-year-old WhatsApp group of friends became the place he goes when he no longer recognizes himself.

He also opens up about being hated in America for more than a year and then loved overnight, and what his younger brother told him about the fans who feel they already know him.

Learn why the roles you took on as a child can become the trap that holds you back. And learn the one question Trevor asks himself to know when it is time to let go.

videos.title: 4 THINGS TO DO TO FALL ASLEEP
videos.description:
Sleep is the foundation of mental health, physical health, and performance. Each of us has different sleep needs but most need between 6-9 hours.

The longer we are awake, the more adenosine builds up in our body and brain. Adenosine promote sleepiness.

Many things inhibit our ability to fall asleep. Caffeine too close to bedtime, room too hot, gnawing hunger, worry etc.

This video explains 4 key things that promote falling asleep. These are things you can control.

1) Core body temperature needs to drop.
The reason a hot bath, shower, or warm compress to the upper face work to lower core body temperature is, after you get out, the medial preoptic nucleus of your hypothalamus, which contains neurons that are sort of like a thermostat, trigger a drop in your core body temp. No hot water? Holding something cool (not ice cold) can help too.

2) Long exhales until your lungs are empty slows your heart down. This is actually the basis of HRV. It’s controlled by a descending branch of your vagus nerve.

3) It’s impossible to turn off your thoughts, but you can shift thinking about the past or plans or worries to your immediate sensations at the level of your skin inward (interoception).

4) “Rocking” slowly back-and-forth triggers reflexive eye movements that in turn help falling asleep. It’s because those eye movements turn off a set of circuits that pay attention to limb position. But most don’t have beds that allow them to be slowly rocked!

By slowly moving your eyes from side to side (underneath closed eye eyelids), & up and down, many people find they fall (back) asleep. Indeed there are eyemasks being developed that trigger this pattern of eye movements to induce sleep. In the meantime, you can try this trick. Many people find it works. It may not work for you, but it costs nothing and is safe.

videos.title: The Question That Reveals What You Want
videos.description:
A 2019 study of college students looked at what happens when people chase goals that line up with their own values. Over time, those students showed fewer symptoms of anxiety and depression.

Psychologists also have a name for the opposite problem: low values clarity. Not knowing what you care about is linked to aimlessness and weak motivation.

Put those together and you get a useful test for any goal.

A six-pack you want because you value your health can survive a rainy Sunday of meal prep. A six-pack you want so people will look at you differently usually can't. Same goal, same cost. One of them is yours and one of them is borrowed.

That's why so many plans fall apart in week three. The reward was imagined in vivid detail. The value underneath it was never there.

You don't need more willpower for a borrowed goal. You need a different goal.

Pick one goal you say you want. Write down what it costs you every single week. Then ask whose value it serves. If the answer isn't yours, you just saved yourself a year.

videos.title: Trusting Nobody Makes You Easy to Fool
videos.description:
Watch Chapter 4 of Manipulation, Solved to learn why trusting no one might actually make you easier to manipulate.

Being skeptical of everything might feel like a form of self-protection, but chronic distrust can have the opposite effect. When you stop trusting people altogether, you risk isolating yourself, and that loneliness can make you even more vulnerable to manipulation.
